title: Short-term arrival strategies for endurance exercise performance at moderate altitude
claims: The study compared 14 hours of overnight hypoxic exposure with 2 hours of hypoxic exposure before a 20-km cycling time trial at a simulated 2500 m.
Performance responses diverged between the 14-hour and 2-hour conditions but were not explained by the measured physiological variables.
Athletes restricted to arriving the evening before competition would not gain a clear advantage by delaying arrival to a few hours before the event.
The paper notes that 5-7 days of acclimatisation produced worse performance than 14-19 days, while residence longer than 19 days produced only marginal additional gains.
